reference: GNU coreutils seq, invoked by the same shell script and argv as the candidate; GNU stdout, exit status, and fixture tree are the parity oracle.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and help metadata
One-, two-, and three-operand integer sequences, signed ranges, and non-divisible endpoints
Exact output for small ranges above 64-bit integer precision
Decimal precision, exponent notation, and rounded floating endpoints
Equal-width padding, custom separators, and printf-style format strings
Empty ranges and representative zero-increment, invalid-format, and option errors
exclusions: Interactive, filesystem, privileged, hardware, and network behavior is outside seq's contract; no deferred operation case applies.
Diagnostic wording is not compared because GNU and Bash builtin diagnostics may differ; failures require nonempty stderr.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports seq as a builtin and that its help entry is available. Bash type -t documents the literal builtin result; help is redirected because wording is implementation metadata.
Exercise the one-operand default, two-operand default step, explicit positive step, non-divisible endpoint, and -- before negative operands against GNU seq.
Check descending signed integer sequences and a step that does not land exactly on LAST.
Verify short ranges above 64-bit integer precision preserve every decimal digit. GNU coreutils seq is the independent oracle for these exact operands.
Check operand-derived decimal precision, scientific exponent operands, and the rounded final value for a decimal increment.
Check that ranges whose direction cannot reach LAST succeed with no output, while a positive stepped range with an omitted endpoint still emits its values.
Exercise equal-width zero padding with both a conventional range and leading-zero operands, plus a multi-byte separator.
Check custom printf conversion precision, literal prefix/suffix text, escaped percent, and the long format option spelling.
A zero increment is invalid. Require GNU's status 1, empty stdout, and a diagnostic without pinning implementation-specific wording.
A printf format with an integer conversion is outside seq's supported floating conversions and must fail with a diagnostic.
Check an unrecognized option returns GNU seq's error status and produces a diagnostic.
An empty separator preserves the terminal newline; a singleton descending range is emitted once.
Equal-width and explicit formatting conflict before any output.
